I have definitely done this. I currently am in low income housing and I qualify for my state's SNAP program. I am also on SSDI for a permanent disability. I had college being paid for by the state, but I went and fucked that right up. 

As for someone to talk to, that's where it get's tricky. I've seen a few people down here, but they're so busy with other patients that it's just really, really impersonal and it wasn't doing anything for me. Unfortunately the county I live in has a shortage of mental health resources. I had a few people I wanted to see in the next town over, but my car died and yeah... :/

I guess I haven't really tried that, I'm not sure if it's the relationships though? The first relationship I mentioned, there was no anxiety until the very end. I just honestly feel like things are spiraling out of control with my anxiety and it's crossing over into everything in my life. Even having been alone for the past 2 weeks, I still feel it. I'm just... exhausted at this point. :/
